# Freemap.sk

> Freemap.sk is a map application built on OpenStreetMap data by the NGO Freemap Slovakia (a Slovak local chapter of the OpenStreetMap Foundation), used in the browser and as a mobile app for Android and iOS. It serves everyday use (finding places, routing by car, bike or on foot, weather), outdoor trips (its own detailed outdoor map of Europe with waymarked trails and terrain relief, elevation profiles, panoramas, offline maps), and work with maps that comes close to a GIS (custom terrain shading, drawing and measuring, file conversion, custom WMS/tile maps, viewshed, isochrones, print and 3D-print export). Most of it is free to use; an optional paid premium tier funds the service and unlocks extras. This file gives AI systems and assistants structured information so they can explain, describe, and help users interact with the site.

Contact: [freemap@freemap.sk](mailto:freemap@freemap.sk); mobile apps for Android and iOS: [mobileapp@freemap.sk](mailto:mobileapp@freemap.sk)

Key facts:

- Built on OpenStreetMap data; the map is continuously updated from the OSM database, so an OSM edit shows within minutes.
- Most of the app is free to use. An optional yearly premium tier (15 €) and prepaid credits unlock extras: high-resolution elevation data, the finer panorama and viewshed renders, multimodal routing, breaks and overnights on a route, most colorize modes, and premium photos. Open source; no user tracking.
- Maps: the own **Outdoor** map of 46 European countries with marked hiking, bicycle, ski and riding trails in their waymark colours; terrain relief from national high-resolution terrain models in 18 countries (30 m elsewhere); **parametric terrain shading** of Europe, designed by the user from layers (hillshade, slope, colour relief, contours) or presets; aerial imagery; a library of over 1,400 more maps from the Editor Layer Index (aerial, historic and national maps), plus the user's own WMS, tile and vector maps, stacked with opacity and saved as presets.
- Overlays: community photos (over 700,000, including 360° panoramas) and over 30 million geotagged Wikimedia Commons photos; Wikipedia articles; events (shared trips, nearly 3,000 upcoming, most harvested from hiking-club and tourism calendars); OSM notes; an animated weather radar; viewshed.
- Search: places, addresses, coordinates, OSM elements, POIs by category, events, and the app's own functions and maps.
- Route finder: 13 travel profiles (car, toll-free car, 4WD, motorcycle, walking, hiking, easy hike, stroller/wheelchair, bicycle, MTB, gravel, road bike, e-bike) plus a straight line, a different one per part of a route, departure time and itinerary with breaks and overnights at stops, weather along the route at the time of passing, alternatives, round trips, optimized stop order, isochrones.
- Routes, tracks and live tracks can be colorized by what is known along them — from the map data (elevation, steepness, surface, road type, hiking and MTB difficulty, waymark colour) and, for recorded tracks, from the recording (speed, heart rate, cadence, power, …); 18 modes in all, with a matching elevation profile.
- Weather: an hourly 16-day forecast for any place in Europe, as lists or charts; weather radar.
- Drawing and data: points, lines and polygons with styles, properties and label templates; measuring length, area, azimuth and position; importing, editing (join, split, simplify, match to roads) and converting GPX, KML/KMZ, TCX and GeoJSON.
- Views: 360° terrain panorama with named peaks, toposcope, viewshed.
- Keeping and sharing: saved personal maps (opened on any device, shared by link, edited together, flagged for offline use), events with participants and discussion, live tracking of phones and GPS trackers with shareable watch links, GPS track recording on Android, embed code for other websites.
- Export: GPX, GeoJSON, KML/KMZ (also to Google Drive, Dropbox and Garmin Connect); map images and documents as PDF, SVG, PNG, WebP and JPEG; offline maps as MBTiles/SQLiteDB; terrain models for 3D printing as STL, or 3MF with the route, drawings and landcover in colour.
- Offline: an installable web app that starts and works without a connection, downloaded offline maps, tile caching while browsing.
- UI in 9 languages: Slovak, Czech, English, German, Hungarian, Polish, Italian, Slovenian, French.
- The application is a single-page application (SPA) and reflects its state in the URL; it registers WebMCP tools for AI agents in the browser.

Only the summary and the deep-link reference are in this file. Everything else — the application's functions (the main-menu tools and modals) and the available map layers — is in the reference files listed below, one fetch each.

## Deep links (building map URLs)

The app keeps its state in the URL, so you can hand a user a link that opens Freemap in a specific state — a viewport, chosen layers, markers, drawn lines/areas, a planned route, or an opened modal — with no API and no login. This is the normal way to "create a map" programmatically: build the URL and give it to the user.

Parameters live in the URL **hash** (`#name=value&name2=value2…`); a query string (`?name=…`) is accepted as a fallback. Base URL: `https://www.freemap.sk/`.

The highest-value parameters for building links:

- `map=zoom/lat/lon` — viewport, e.g. `map=13/48.7483/19.1480` (coordinates to 6 decimals). With a fractional **Zoom step**, the zoom can be fractional too, to 2 decimals (`map=13.75/…`).
- `layers=codes` — base layer + overlays by their id code (see the layer registry in [Map Layers](/llms-layers.md)), e.g. `layers=X` (Outdoor) or `layers=X~I` (Outdoor + Photos). A custom map the link carries is named here by its id too, in its place in the stack, and so is an offline map, which only the device holding it can show. A `layers=` naming nothing the app knows leaves the map as it is.
- `l.<code>=fields` — one layer's setup, for a layer in `layers=`; fields are `;`-separated, each a letter and a value: `kb`/`ko` base or overlay (any map but the data layers used as the other kind), `o<percent>` opacity, `w<names>` the WMS layers drawn (each URI-encoded, `,`-separated), `s<shading>` the terrain shading, `c<rrggbbaa>` the solid colour. E.g. `layers=X~WKA&l.WKA=ko;o60` lays the cadastre over Outdoor at 60%. A layer in `layers=` without one opens with its defaults. The older `shading=` is read as the setup of `h`.
- `@<n>` in `layers=` and `p.<n>=codes` — a map preset carried in the link: `p.<n>` lists its maps bottom first, `~`-joined; `p.<n>.n=` its name, `p.<n>.i=` its icon, `p.<n>.o=` its opacity in %, and `p.<n>.l.<code>=` each of its maps' opacity and kind as above; a map's WMS layers, shading or colour are its own, in `l.<code>=`, even for a map drawn only in presets. E.g. `layers=S~@1&p.1=xh~xb&p.1.n=Trails&p.1.o=70` lays a preset of hiking and bicycle trails over aerial imagery at 70%; a preset holding a base map takes the base map's place. A lone preset is written `layers=@1~`.
- **`point=lat/lon` — put a marker on the map. This is the parameter for "a map with points / markers". It is repeatable: add one `point=` per marker.**
- `line=lat/lon,lat/lon,…` and `polygon=lat/lon,lat/lon,…` — draw a line or a filled area (each repeatable).
- `points=[transport/]lat/lon,…` together with `transport=…` — a **planned route** through waypoints. This is routing, not standalone markers — do not confuse the plural `points=` with the marker parameter `point=`.
- `show=type[/arg]` — open a modal/viewer, e.g. `show=gallery-viewer/123`.
- `elevation-chart=feature` — open the elevation profile on the feature named: `route-planner` (the planned route), `track-viewer` (the active line of Drawing and data — the first line when the link is opened), or `tracking/<deviceToken>` (a tracked device); the older `drawing/<lineIndex>` is read as `track-viewer`. Only one profile shows at a time, and it opens once the geometry it charts has loaded — so it can be combined with `points=`, `track-uid=`, `import-url=` or a saved map's `id=`.
- `elevation-chart-range=<from>,<to>` — the stretch of that profile marked out for its own figures, in whole metres along it. Ignored without an `elevation-chart=`, and dropped where the profile turns out shorter than it.
- `route-colorize-by=mode`, `track-colorize-by=mode`, `tracking-colorize-by=mode` — what the planned route, the loaded track, or the tracked devices are colored by: `elevation`, `steepness`, `surface`, `smoothness`, `roadType`, `trackType`, `hikeRating`, `mtbRating`, `trailColor`, `speed`, `heartRate`, `cadence`, `power`, `temperature`, `time`, `heading`, `battery`, `gsmSignal`. A mode the feature has no data for simply paints nothing, and an unknown name is ignored. Since the elevation profile takes its colors from the same setting, this colors the chart too.
- `route-colorize-legend=1|0`, `track-colorize-legend=1|0`, `tracking-colorize-legend=1|0` — whether that feature's legend, the box naming what the colors mean, is shown. Written only alongside a mode, since the legend appears only while one is active; omitted, the reader's own preference stands (it defaults to shown).
- `route-params-hash=key` — carries a **premium route feature to someone without premium**: multimodal segmentation, and the premium colorize modes. It is the key of the route the link was made for, so it applies to that route alone and lapses as soon as a waypoint moves — the reader sees the feature on the shared route, never on one of their own. Written only while the route already has those features (a premium user's, or a shared one being passed on), so a link cannot be made to grant what its author did not have.
- `panel=kind/id` — what is selected with a panel of its own, one at a time: `panel=event/<id>` (an event, turning the **Events** layer on), `panel=osm-note/<id>` (an OSM note), `panel=changeset/<id>` (a changeset inspected, as clicking it does), `panel=changeset/<id>/<node|way|relation>/<id>` (with one of its changed elements selected), `panel=osm-<node|way|relation>/<id>` (an OSM element, kept by `osm-*=` or only looked at, which then leaves the map when deselected) `panel=object/<node|way|relation>/<id>` (a POI of the objects layer, selected once `objects=` has loaded it; either OSM form with `/history` appended shows the element's versions), `panel=weather/<lat>,<lon>` (the weather forecast for a place) and `panel=wiki/<lang>:<title>` (a Wikipedia article's preview; older links' `show=wiki/…` still open it). `osm-*=` alone puts the elements on the map without selecting any, except in a query string (`https://www.freemap.sk/?layers=X&osm-node=<id>`), which opens the first one's panel. Older links' `event=<id>`, `osm-note=<id>` and `changeset=<id>` still open the same. `follow=<token>` keeps the map on a watched device's position, apart from any selection (see [Live tracking](/llms-tracking.md)).
- `lang=code` — force the UI language (`en`, `sk`, …).

**Example — a map with two markers** (Bratislava and Košice) on the Outdoor layer:

```
https://www.freemap.sk/#map=8/48.43/19.18&layers=X&point=48.14816/17.10674&point=48.72083/21.25808
```

**Styling, labelling and opening the editor.** After the `lat/lon`, a `point` / `line` / `polygon` value may carry style fields, each a one-letter code, joined by the record-separator `%1E` (a leading `%1E` separates them from the coordinates). The useful codes are `L`abel, `C`olor (`%23` = `#`, RGBA hex), `S`hape (`s`quare / `r`ing, default pin), and `I`con spec — `poi:<name>` for a bundled POI icon or `fa:<name>` for a Font Awesome icon (`%3A` = `:`). The markers show on their own; `tools=draw-points` is optional and only additionally opens the drawing toolbar so the user can edit the points. E.g. a blue ring marker labelled "Ahoj!" with the animal-shelter icon:

```
https://www.freemap.sk/#map=17/48.979457/21.169961&layers=X&tools=draw-points&point=48.979061/21.167738%1EC%230000ff%1ELAhoj!%1ESr%1EIpoi%3Aanimal_shelter
```

For every URL parameter and the full style codec, see [`doc/url-params.md`](https://github.com/FreemapSlovakia/freemap-v3-react/blob/main/doc/url-params.md).

## Reference files

Each is a Markdown fragment of this document, continuing its heading levels. Together they describe every function and map layer. The functions are reached from the main menu, under a button with a "hamburger" icon at the top left of the page.

- [Interface, search and account](/llms-interface.md): the search box (places, coordinates, OSM elements, the app's own functions), the UI language and theme switchers, the account with purchases, premium, credits, login providers and app tokens, user profiles, clearing the map, the help documents and legend, and the map context menu.
- [Photos and personal maps](/llms-photos-maps.md): the community photo layer, uploading and rating photos, the leaderboard, saved personal maps (sharing, offline flagging, writing back), and events (saved maps published as shared trips).
- [Drawing and data](/llms-drawing.md): the one collection of points, lines and polygons — drawn, imported from GPX/GeoJSON/KML/KMZ/TCX files, or brought in from elsewhere — how it is kept (in the link or in the browser), editing, styles and labels, colorizing, matching, measurement, and the elevation profile.
- [Routes and tracks](/llms-routes-tracks.md): the route finder (transport modes, waypoints, alternatives, isochrones, colorizing, elevation profile).
- [OpenStreetMap objects, details and changes](/llms-osm.md): searching POIs by category, the map-details panel for an OSM element, the recent-changes viewer, and the OSM notes overlay.
- [Live tracking and the GPS recorder](/llms-tracking.md): tracked devices, watched devices, access tokens, and the standalone Android GPS recorder the app drives.
- [Toposcope and panorama](/llms-views.md): the printable direction dial of surrounding summits, and the 360° terrain render with its peak names, distances and quality steps.
- [Weather](/llms-weather.md): the hourly weather forecast for a place (days, hours and charts) and the animated weather radar.
- [Offline use](/llms-offline.md): what works without a connection and where settings are kept, downloaded offline maps, and caching tiles while browsing.
- [Sharing and export](/llms-export.md): sharing a link or opening the place in another app, exporting the map as an image or document, exporting map data, maps for GPS devices, exporting an offline map, and the embed code.
- [Map Layers](/llms-layers.md): the map toolbar and the full layer registry with each layer's id code, zoom range, coverage and credits.
- [Manage maps](/llms-manage-maps.md): the map manager — installed maps (each map's toolbar, menu, opacity and shortcut settings) and available maps (searching, previewing and installing maps), custom maps, layer setups, the Map layers panel, map presets, map and elevation preferences.
- [In-page agent tools (WebMCP)](/llms-agent-tools.md): the tools the app registers on `document.modelContext` for an AI agent running in the user's browser.
